content.comment_body: On the website demo software, upgrades/updates, and drivers, the [product_name] software [version_no] is available for download.

I've downloaded the software, but when I launch the installer it greets me with 'Hello, welcome to installer [version_no]'. It seems the link might be incorrect. Has anyone successfully downloaded [version_no]? Also, is there any information on the new features in this release? I can't find any details.
I downloaded and installed the upgrade. The installer displayed [version_no], and after completing installation, the 'Info... about' section in [product_name] also reports [version_no].
I downloaded both update files—32-bit and 64-bit. After installation, the 64-bit file shows it is [version_no], while the 32-bit file shows [version_no]!
I've tried to obtain the latest (64-bit) version, but only receive [version_no]. Perhaps someone attempted to resolve the issue. The checksums also don't match.
When I download the upgrade to [version_no] (64-bit), see attachment.
And here is the upgrade for [version_no] (32-bit):

This is quite unusual. When trying to download the 64-bit software, the file offered is 132MB instead of 157MB. The 32-bit version is offered at 154MB as expected. Could possible rerouting of servers cause this? Updating directly through the [product_name] software doesn't work.
I am experiencing the exact same issue. The SHA256 checksum matches the previously mentioned one (ending in 392525), and upon installation, it shows [version_no] instead of [version_no].

It looks like everything has synchronized now. This morning, clicking the download link provides a 157MB file, [product_name] [version_no]. One problem: Windows 10 SmartScreen blocks the installation.

Hello, either the provided checksum is incorrect or the setup.bin file for the 32-bit Linux version is corrupted or replaced without updating the checksum. After downloading multiple times from [url], the linux command sha256sum gives the checksum [binary_data_removed], whereas it should be [binary_data_removed] according to [company_name]. I am confident sha256sum is functioning properly. For the 64-bit version, both published and calculated checksums match. Would appreciate if someone could download the 32-bit Linux setup file, calculate its sha256 checksum, and share both the result and the tools used (OS, checksum utility). Best regards [user_name]
Hello, it is now confirmed that the checksum published by [company_name] was incorrect; see related German post at [url]. Best regards
I need the 32-bit and 64-bit update files. I believe the link is no longer available—could someone share the files if previously downloaded?

Hello [user_name], this website is no longer supported by [company_name]. A download link for [product_name] [version_no] is now available. You can download the complete package for [version_no] SP1 here: [product_name] [version_no] SP1 (download, notes, instructions). The full package size is 1.3 GB.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are experiencing inconsistencies when downloading and installing [product_name] [version_no]. Many report receiving files and installers labeled as [version_no], rather than the advertised [version_no]. Both 32-bit and 64-bit downloads show differences in file size and checksum mismatches, suggesting potential issues with file integrity or distribution from the [company_name] website. Attempting updates via built-in software functionality is also unsuccessful for several users.
analysis.user_expectations: Users anticipate being able to download and install the advertised latest version, [product_name] [version_no], with clearly reported version details and consistent updates across both 32-bit and 64-bit files.
